items.title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday, FAA head says
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 14 (Reuters) - US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry. ET (0235 GMT), airlines on Saturday had ‌canceled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website.

items.title: Duffy Probing Possible L3Harris ‘Incompetence’ in FAA Meltdown
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that officials are looking into whether aerospace and defense contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. was at fault for an aviation traffic control system shutdown that grounded flights nationwide for more than four hours.

items.title: Duffy Says an L3Harris Crew Was Working on the FAA Network When Flights Stopped. Its Stock Fell 4% After Hours
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an L3Harris crew was switching FAA lines from copper wire to fiber when a router flooded the air traffic control network. L3Harris fell 4.2% after hours, and airlines owe stranded travelers nothing.

items.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at US airports and triggered the longest shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks.
